q: Which is the right way to store passwords?
o: Hashed with a slow, memory-hard function like Argon2id plus a unique salt
why: Fast hashes can be brute-forced; encryption can be reversed with the key.

q: What does a per-user salt prevent?
o: Precomputed (rainbow table) attacks and spotting users with the same password
why: Same password, different salt, different hash.

q: Forcing users to change their password every 90 days is current NIST advice.
why: Myth. Modern NIST guidance drops forced periodic changes; change only on evidence of compromise, and check new passwords against breach lists.
